title: Why a 50 percent rise then a 50 percent fall doesn't get you back
examples: Does a 50% rise then a 50% fall cancel out?
Why is 100 up 50% then down 50% only 75?

explain.say: A pair of trainers costs 100 dollars. Look at the first bar. The shop puts the price up by 50 percent, then has a 50 percent sale. Are you back at 100? Most people say yes. Let us check.

explain.say: Of the new price, 150! Half of 150 is 75. So the trainers end at 75 dollars, not 100. Look how much shorter the last bar is.

explain.say: You spotted a trap many adults fall into. Well done! Wow: after a 50 percent fall, you need a 100 percent rise to get back. Challenge: a price falls by 20 percent. What rise brings it back?

faq.q: Why is the final price lower than the start?
faq.a: The 50 percent fall is taken from the higher price, 150 dollars. So it takes away 75 dollars, more than the 50 dollars that was added.

faq.q: What is the base of a percentage?
faq.a: The base is the amount the percentage is taken from. In a percentage change, it is the value just before that change.

faq.q: What rise undoes a 20 percent fall?
faq.a: A 20 percent fall leaves 80. To get back to 100 you add 20, which is a quarter of 80. So you need a 25 percent rise.
asks: How do you reverse a 20% decrease?

faq.q: Does the order matter, rise first or fall first?
faq.a: No. 100 times 0.5 times 1.5 is also 75. Multiplying works in any order.
asks: Is it different if the sale comes first?

faq.q: How do I work out two percentage changes in a row?
faq.a: Multiply by both multipliers. A 10 percent rise then a 10 percent fall is 1.1 times 0.9, which is 0.99. That is 1 percent less than you started with.

facts: A 10% rise followed by a 10% fall leaves 99% of the start, because 1.1 × 0.9 = 0.99.
To recover from a 50% fall, a value must rise by 100%.

quiz.say: A share price of 200 goes up 10 percent, then down 10 percent. What is it now?

wrong.1: 200 assumes the changes cancel, but the fall is taken from 220.

quiz.say: A price falls by 50 percent. What percentage rise brings it back?
quiz.why: After a 50 percent fall you have half, so you must double it. That is a 100 percent rise.

wrong.1: A 50 percent rise on half only gets back to three quarters.
wrong.2: 150 percent goes too far, to one and a quarter times the start.
